item.title: Update: A pre-auth RCE chain in PaperCut NG/MF was exploited before any patch existed; tested maintenance releases now replace three emergency patches
item.description: Hunt.io recovered the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) and reports a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API that does not use the Tapestry bypass and works when the API allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, an offline LSA-secret playbook and 45 victims with live internal pivots, Switzerland among the countries listed. Hunt.io does not report the XML-RPC route used against a victim; PaperCut's documentation names the token and allowlist settings that close it. PaperCut's September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 and names 24.1.11 as the v24 build.
item.content:encoded:
Update17 Oct 2026 03:38 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-inteltitlesummaryregionstechniquescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Hunt.io recovered the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) and reports a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API that does not use the Tapestry bypass and works when the API allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, an offline LSA-secret playbook and 45 victims with live internal pivots, Switzerland among the countries listed. Hunt.io does not report the XML-RPC route used against a victim; PaperCut's documentation names the token and allowlist settings that close it. PaperCut's September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 and names 24.1.11 as the v24 build.

Hunt.io found three open directories on one attacker host and reconstructs the operator's toolkit from the files in them; it says the recovered material aligns with GreyNoise's published account of the AI-driven campaign (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). The operator's notes record a second route to code execution that does not use the Tapestry bypass: PaperCut's XML-RPC API at /rpc/api/xmlrpc accepts api.setConfigValue when its network allowlist is too permissive or no explicit API token is configured, because the handler then falls back to the built-in admin password as the token, and the same user-lookup settings are then rewritten (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). Hunt.io says an instance already hardened against the Tapestry bypass is not necessarily protected against this one if its XML-RPC API is exposed with weak access controls (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15); it does not report the route used against a victim. PaperCut's documentation says the API's authentication token should be defined in the advanced config key auth.webservices.auth-token and that the address allowlist can be set in the admin interface or through auth.webservices.allowed-addresses (PaperCut Software, 2026-01-30).

The files also show what follows a compromise. A Linux kit keeps a chisel reverse SOCKS5 client alive through cron entries (periodic and at reboot) and a watchdog script that checks the process (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). The Windows playbook exports the SECURITY and SYSTEM registry hives from a compromised host to recover LSA secrets, the domain machine account's password among them, offline (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). The scale comes from the actor's own files: a reconnaissance pool of 1,005 hosts in at least 45 countries (800 confirmed vulnerable and 205 flagged from version fingerprinting), 2,165 logged attempts, 46 Active Directory domains packaged as victim data and 45 targets with a live reverse SOCKS5 pivot at the time of capture (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). Switzerland is among the countries listed for those 45 targets, with no sector or organisation named, and Hunt.io says it shared its findings and the victim data with the national CERTs of the affected countries (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15).

PaperCut's September security bulletin, last updated 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 on the 24.x branch as well as in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13, and recommends 26.0.5, 25.0.13 or 24.1.11 or later (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-24).

Open finding: CVE-2026-82078 / CVE-2026-81578, PaperCut NG/MF: an Apache Tapestry request-routing confusion chains an unauthenticated config rewrite to arbitrary code execution, exploited before a patch existed →

item.title: Update: Exchange October updates fix an unauthenticated email-borne RCE; 2016 and 2019 get their last update, and only with ESU
item.description: Microsoft's Exchange Team now gives a workaround for the instability that the October 2026 Windows Server updates can cause on Exchange servers: it advises against uninstalling them and says setting the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap to 65536 and rebooting has solved the cases it assisted. It adds that DAG members losing quorum are among the reported symptoms and that the Exchange security updates are not the cause.
item.content:encoded:
Update17 Oct 2026 03:36 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidenceactionsbody

Microsoft's Exchange Team now gives a workaround for the instability that the October 2026 Windows Server updates can cause on Exchange servers: it advises against uninstalling them and says setting the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap to 65536 and rebooting has solved the cases it assisted. It adds that DAG members losing quorum are among the reported symptoms and that the Exchange security updates are not the cause.

Microsoft's Exchange Team has published guidance for Exchange servers that become unstable after the October 2026 Windows Server updates. Since 2026-10-13 it has seen reports of OWA failing with MapiExceptionMdbOffline (hr=0x80004005, ec=1142; event ID 1006 in the Application log), mail queues growing during the day, DAG members unable to reach quorum and a reboot helping only temporarily; Exchange 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition can all be affected (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17). It says the issues are not related to installing the October 2026 Exchange security updates and that any Exchange version running on an affected Windows build can be hit; KB5126646 (Windows Server 2025), KB5126655 (2022), KB5126651 (2019) and KB5126868 (2016) can cause the failures after some time, and the impact varies with Exchange load, so some servers may never see a problem (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Microsoft's recommendation is not to uninstall the October 2026 Windows Server updates and, from an elevated command prompt on the Exchange server, to set the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Rpc to 65536, reboot, monitor, and raise the limit if the problem recurs; it says this has solved the customer cases it has assisted (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Open finding: CVE-2026-70571, Microsoft Exchange Server: an unauthenticated crafted-email code-execution flaw in the October 2026 security updates, the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 updates under the paid ESU (CVSS 8.1) →

item.title: Update: PK Softech: the City of Zurich pension fund confirms its test data was stolen; Pensionskasse Post says data left
item.description: The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, now says in its notice of 2026-10-15 that its inquiries indicate personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch, was stolen, and that which fields were taken is still being clarified. Pensionskasse Post says in its notice of the same date that personal data did leave and no longer repeats its earlier anonymisation statement, though it is still unclear whether its insured persons' data is among it.
item.content:encoded:
Update17 Oct 2026 03:35 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, now says in its notice of 2026-10-15 that its inquiries indicate personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch, was stolen, and that which fields were taken is still being clarified. Pensionskasse Post says in its notice of the same date that personal data did leave and no longer repeats its earlier anonymisation statement, though it is still unclear whether its insured persons' data is among it.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich (PKZH), the City of Zurich's pension fund, has moved from checking to confirming. Its notice of 2026-10-15 says its inquiries so far indicate that personal data of PKZH insured persons was also stolen in the attack, and that this data had been used in tests for the planned system switch (PKZH, 2026-10-15); its FAQ adds that data was taken from PK Softech's system, including personal data of insured persons and of pensioners (PKZH, 2026-10-15). Inside IT reports that PKZH currently uses another software provider and plans to move to PK Softech's system in 2027 (Inside IT, 2026-10-16); PKZH's own FAQ says the system it uses to manage assets and pay pensions is not affected and dates the move to the beginning of 2027 (PKZH, 2026-10-15). The page still carries its earlier line that PKZH is checking whether its data is affected next to the confirmation (PKZH, 2026-10-15). It says a switch of this kind has to be tested with data that reproduces the real pension relationships as completely as possible, that PK Softech is contractually bound to protect and keep the data confidential, and that whether it met that duty is being investigated (PKZH, 2026-10-15).

Which data was stolen is still being clarified; in the worst case the fields are first name, name, date of birth, AHV number, address, private and business e-mail and telephone, insured earnings and retirement assets, civil status, partner details and IBAN (PKZH, 2026-10-15). PKZH was told on 2026-10-13 that data of its insured persons might be affected, has filed a criminal complaint and has reported the incident to the data-protection office (PKZH, 2026-10-15). It says a payout needs a signed written request and an identity check and that a change of bank details is checked additionally, so the data alone cannot trigger one, but that criminals can use it to appear credible (PKZH, 2026-10-15).

Pensionskasse Post's notice of 2026-10-15 says the investigation has shown that personal data did leave, and that it remains unclear whether data of its insured persons is affected, though that is possible (Pensionskasse Post, 2026-10-15). It does not repeat its earlier statement that its data at PK Softech is anonymised, and lists name, address, date of birth, AHV number, contact details, e-mail address and pension data as data that could be affected (Pensionskasse Post, 2026-10-15). The access vector, the actor and any ransom demand are still not public in any source read.

Open finding: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating →

item.title: Improvement: Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure chain: its root step had no fix at disclosure, and it evades the Integrity Checker
item.description: The unfixed root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published 2026-10-15, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates it is exploited in the wild; its description names only 22.8R2.4 as affected, says the step was exploited in the wild in October 2026 and states no fixed build, so scanners, SIEM enrichment and tickets can now follow the step by ID.
item.content:encoded:
Improvement17 Oct 2026 03:34 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryimmediate_actioncvessourcesevidencebody

The unfixed root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published 2026-10-15, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates it is exploited in the wild; its description names only 22.8R2.4 as affected, says the step was exploited in the wild in October 2026 and states no fixed build, so scanners, SIEM enrichment and tickets can now follow the step by ID.

The root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published on 2026-10-15 and rated High on GitHub's advisory database as GHSA-fhw5-mpvj-x89m (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-15). Its description reads "Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2.4 mishandles the manner in which the dsinvoked broker trusts DSCache configuration data, leading to privilege escalation to root, as exploited in the wild in October 2026." (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-15), the same step Volexity describes as abusing the dsinvoked service's trust in the shared DSCache store (Volexity, 2026-10-13).

The record names only 22.8R2.4 as affected and states no fixed build; Volexity wrote that Ivanti was working on a fix for release in the coming weeks (Volexity, 2026-10-13), and no source read says whether any build now fixes it. The Canadian Cyber Centre's bulletin on the Ivanti advisory, updated 2026-10-16, adds that open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-111357 is being exploited in the wild (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-10-13). A scanner, SIEM enrichment rule or ticket can now follow the unfixed step by this ID, and an appliance that was exposed still needs the compromise check above.

Open finding: CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, and the root-escalation step of the chain was unpatched at disclosure (CVSS 8.6) →

item.title: Update: Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 record was rejected on 16 October, but the flaw, its fixes and its exploitation stand
item.description: Atlassian, the assigner, rejected the CVE record for CVE-2026-21589 on 2026-10-16, giving only the generic reason that its publication may have been a false positive or a mistake; ENISA's EUVD record mirrors it and still lists exploitation since 2026-10-15. Atlassian's advisory still uses the ID with the same fixed versions, and no source says why the record was rejected or whether a replacement ID will follow, so tooling keyed on the ID can lose track of an exploited flaw.
item.content:encoded:
Update17 Oct 2026 03:34 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Atlassian, the assigner, rejected the CVE record for CVE-2026-21589 on 2026-10-16, giving only the generic reason that its publication may have been a false positive or a mistake; ENISA's EUVD record mirrors it and still lists exploitation since 2026-10-15. Atlassian's advisory still uses the ID with the same fixed versions, and no source says why the record was rejected or whether a replacement ID will follow, so tooling keyed on the ID can lose track of an exploited flaw.

ENISA's EUVD record EUVD-2026-92807 for CVE-2026-21589, which names Atlassian as the assigner, was updated at 20:39 UTC on 2026-10-16 and now describes the record only as "This CVE's publication may have been a false positive or a mistake. As a result, we have rejected this record." (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-16). The same record still lists exploitation since 2026-10-15 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-16).

The flaw itself is unchanged: Atlassian's advisory, as read on 2026-10-17, still uses the ID, lists the same fixed versions and carries no note of the rejection (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). No source read says why the record was rejected or whether a replacement ID will follow. The consequence is for tooling: a scanner plugin, SIEM enrichment rule or ticket keyed on the ID, or on a feed that drops rejected IDs, can stop reporting a flaw that is exploited, so track it by Atlassian's advisory and the fixed versions above until a replacement ID appears.

Open finding: CVE-2026-21589, Atlassian Data Center: unauthenticated arbitrary file access in every version of eight self-managed products, patch or take them off the internet (CVSS 4.0 9.3) →

item.title: GTIG: AOMEI update files were altered for minutes at a time to push a backdoor; Switzerland among victim countries
item.description: Google's GTIG and ManageEngine's METAL report that a cluster tracked as UNC7017 altered two configuration files on AOMEI's update servers for five to ten minutes at a time between April and July 2026, so any Backupper or AnyViewer client that polled during a window downloaded and ran the CROSSROAD downloader, which installed the SHINYROAD backdoor beside a signed Radmin binary. No software flaw is involved, GTIG names Switzerland among 11 victim countries, and the vendor's server-side repair does not clean a host that already ran the downloader, so installations need an endpoint hunt covering April to July 2026.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHNATOB1

AOMEI Backupper and AnyViewer update files tampered with for five to ten minutes at a time between April and July 2026 to push the CROSSROAD downloader and the SHINYROAD backdoor, with Switzerland among 11 countries GTIG names

GTIG and Mandiant report that a cluster they track as UNC7017 repeatedly altered two configuration files on AOMEI Technology's update servers between April and July 2026, each time for five to ten minutes before restoring the genuine content; GTIG confirmed three windows and says more probably went unseen (GTIG, 2026-10-16). ManageEngine's Threat Analysis Lab (METAL) writes "There was no CVE, no memory corruption, and no unpatched component." (METAL, 2026-10-16).

The client polls down_html.ini (update archive address and MD5 checksum) and Notifycfg.ini (what to display and run); during a window the actor pointed the first at an attacker-controlled ZIP with a matching checksum and padded the second with more than 35,000 lines of dummy sections, so the client started the unpacked downloader from its html directory, and GTIG describes the same flow for AnyViewer (GTIG, 2026-10-16). METAL's EDR recorded the chain on Backupper 8.3.0 (METAL, 2026-10-16).

The downloader, CROSSROAD, stops in some branches when the host geolocates to China (GTIG, 2026-10-16) and, METAL adds, when specific endpoint security agents are present (METAL, 2026-10-16). It registers a scheduled task that runs a signed Radmin binary every three hours; that binary loads an attacker-built DLL by search-order hijacking, which registers an in-process COM server running the SHINYROAD backdoor as encrypted PocketPy bytecode (GTIG, 2026-10-16). On some hosts GTIG later saw the Adaptix C2 agent, disguised as Nitro PDF tooling and started by hidden PowerShell through a second scheduled task (GTIG, 2026-10-16). The 20 July window also pointed a popup at a remote WebDAV path through an invisible window, which can leak the user's NetNTLMv2 response (GTIG, 2026-10-16).

GTIG's telemetry shows affected IT-services, telecommunications and higher-education organizations in 11 countries including Switzerland and calls the targeting opportunistic; AOMEI told Mandiant on 2026-07-29 that it had taken corrective action (GTIG, 2026-10-16). AOMEI's Backupper release notes through 8.5.0 list no change to update verification as of 2026-10-17 (AOMEI Technology, 2026-10-09).

Exposure
Windows hosts running AOMEI Backupper or AnyViewer that polled for updates during an unseen window between April and July 2026; server-side repair does not clean a host that already ran the downloader (GTIG, 2026-10-16).
Detection
In process telemetry, an executable written into the Tmphtml or html folders and started by the notification process, and a signed Radmin binary loading an unexpected DLL (GTIG, 2026-10-16); METAL adds dllhost.exe hosting a COM component registered from a non-standard path (METAL, 2026-10-16). Also scheduled tasks named RadminComponentRuntime or NitroRuntime, and outbound SMB (TCP 445) and WebDAV to external addresses; hunt the whole April to July span and preserve the cached update files in the Tmphtml folder (GTIG, 2026-10-16).

Triage: do not validate an alert by fetching AOMEI's update address now: the files revert within minutes and the genuine content served then has led analysts to dismiss real detections; the Nitro PDF camouflage can make alerts read as isolated user downloads, so trace each one's parent process back to the updater (GTIG, 2026-10-16). Radmin is legitimate software, so provenance discriminates: METAL's EDR recorded the updater's unsigned child process installing it (METAL, 2026-10-16).

Defender takeaway
Hunt every Windows host that runs AOMEI Backupper or AnyViewer for these artifacts even though AOMEI says its servers are repaired, treat a match as a compromised host, and block outbound SMB and WebDAV to external addresses, which GTIG advises against NTLM credential coercion (GTIG, 2026-10-16).

item.title: Unit 42: a memory-resident FortiGate implant rides an exploited FortiOS flaw that has no fix on 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4
item.description: Unit 42 describes a September 2024 intrusion at a telecommunications organization, tracked as CL-STA-0954 (UNC5820), that began with the FortiManager flaw CVE-2024-47575, exfiltrated the configurations and cryptographic material of more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and later used the FortiOS CLI auto-script path traversal CVE-2025-61624 to install PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 implant that patches the logging and IPsec daemons in memory and leaves no persistent binary on disk. Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-122 of 2026-04-14 lists CVE-2025-61624 as known exploited and gives no fix for FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, only a move to a fixed release, so those branches stay exposed to an attacker who already holds a privileged administrator account.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2025-61624exploitedNATOB2

PEERSTITCH: a memory-resident FortiGate implant installed through the FortiOS CLI path traversal CVE-2025-61624, which Fortinet lists as exploited and leaves unfixed on FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, after a FortiManager compromise exposed the configurations of 500+ firewalls

Unit 42 investigated a September 2024 intrusion at a telecommunications organization, tracked as cluster CL-STA-0954, that began with CVE-2024-47575 against a centralized FortiManager appliance: the attackers registered a rogue virtual FortiGate, then exfiltrated an archive with the running configurations, cryptographic material and database files of more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Unit 42 recovered the configurations' reversible-ciphertext credentials by brute force; the attackers later logged in over SSL VPN with legitimate credentials and pushed packet-capture settings to downstream firewalls (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

For root they used CVE-2025-61624, a path traversal in the FortiOS CLI system.auto-script engine that lets an authenticated administrative account read and write arbitrary files as root (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). That installed PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 injector that attaches with ptrace to the logging daemon miglogd and the IPsec daemon iked, allocates a 16 KB read-write-execute region, NOP-patches three fixed offsets and links the daemons through /proc memory so that tagged VPN sessions skip default FortiOS validation; it leaves no persistent binary on disk, opens no listening port and makes no outbound connection of its own (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Command and control ran through the firewall's own Apache mod_md ACME module, whose DNS-01 challenge handler executes Node.js with parameters from an attacker-run ACME server and so opens a reverse shell (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-122 of 2026-04-14 covers the CLI path traversal in FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy and FortiSwitchManager, lists it as known exploited, and for FortiOS gives fixes only in 7.6.5 and 7.4.10, telling users of 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4 to migrate to a fixed release (Fortinet, 2026-04-14).

Exposure
FortiOS on 7.2, 7.0 or 6.4, which have no fixed build, or on 7.6.0 to 7.6.4 and 7.4.0 to 7.4.9, with administrators who can reach the CLI (Fortinet, 2026-04-14); and a FortiManager below 7.6.1, 7.4.5, 7.2.8, 7.0.13, 6.4.15 or 6.2.13 that is reachable on TCP 541 from untrusted networks, where the intrusion began (Fortinet, 2024-10-23; Unit 42, 2026-10-14).
Detection
Management-plane audit records of the FortiManager (device registrations, archive creation, TCP 541 sessions from outside the management network); FortiGate administrator and VPN logs for SSL VPN logins with valid credentials from new external addresses and for administrator accounts that match nobody in the estate, such as an unexpected FortiGateCloud account; gaps in forwarded syslog, because the actors stop the logging daemons before running scripts; and unexplained packet-capture settings (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Unit 42's hunting guidance adds the memory maps of miglogd and iked (anonymous 16,384-byte rwxp regions), text-segment integrity at three fixed offsets, cross-process open and write on /proc/<pid>/mem, signal-11 crashes of miglogd, iked or syslogd in the crash log, and configuration revisions holding auto-script objects with ../ in the name (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Triage: legitimate FortiManager work also creates and deletes auto-scripts and adds devices; the report's signals are ../ in an auto-script name, a device registered from outside the management network, and accounts that match no administrator or tenant the organization created.

Defender takeaway
Plan the move off FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, where Fortinet offers no fix for an exploited root escalation (Fortinet, 2026-04-14), and limit who can reach the administrative CLI meanwhile; after any suspected FortiManager compromise treat every managed device's credentials and certificates as compromised and rotate them, because the stolen trust material stays valid until it is rotated (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Builds on: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed is still active, locks admins out of FortiGates and feeds…

item.title: Unit 42: government Linux web and mail hosts hit with PHP prepend persistence, a sudo password trap and mail searches
item.description: Unit 42 reports CL-UNK-1211, a cluster of unknown nation-state or criminal affiliation that between October 2025 and April 2026 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure, focusing on Linux servers to run reconnaissance and keep persistent access for intelligence collection. Its scripts carry AI-style reasoning comments, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work; the intrusions used PHP web shells with auto_prepend_file persistence on Plesk hosts, a replaced .bashrc that traps sudo passwords, SUID root shells, searches of mail directories and log cleanup. Unit 42 names no victim or country, does not say how the web shells were first placed, and is the only source.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

CL-UNK-1211: an AI-assisted intrusion set against government Linux web and mail servers persists through PHP auto_prepend_file, steals sudo passwords with a fake prompt and reads mail stores, and tries to pass as a red-team exercise

Unit 42 reports a campaign it tracks as CL-UNK-1211 (UNK: affiliation undetermined) against government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure between October 2025 and April 2026, concentrating on Linux servers for persistent access and intelligence collection (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). It names no victim or country and does not say how the web shells were first placed; the recovered tools include a custom Go scanner for CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell) (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). The scripts carry conversational, step-by-step comments in the style of an AI model, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work, an inference rather than a confirmed finding (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).

On the hosts, the attackers ran PHP web shells under the php-fpm parent process and rewrote auto_prepend_file in every PHP configuration under /etc/php/ and /opt/plesk/php/, so a planted file runs first (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). They replaced a .bashrc with a copy that, in one instance, aliases sudo to a fake password prompt that logs the input, searched configuration and history files for credentials, escalated with LinPEAS and the public PwnKit exploit (CVE-2021-4034), left root-SUID shells under hidden names and injected an SSH key into authorized_keys (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). They moved laterally with sshpass and hard-coded credentials and through an MSSQL double hop using xp_cmdshell, and kept access with SysGoRAT, a Go trojan that takes commands over WebSocket, plus the revsocks and pysoxy proxies and GSocket's gs-netcat, which ran from /dev/shm under a fake kernel-thread process name (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). On government mail servers they enumerated /var/qmail/mailnames/, counted mails in Maildir folders to pick targets and searched mail headers for social-media messages; they tried to exfiltrate database dumps over netcat and to public file-hosting platforms, to delete authentication, history, mail and system logs and to kill endpoint security processes, timestomped scripts with touch -t, and planted a red-team marker string and a pentest-style password to pass as an authorised exercise (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Linux web and mail hosting estates of government or state-affiliated bodies, in particular Plesk-managed PHP stacks and their /var/qmail/mailnames/ mail directories, which the attackers enumerated and searched; the report does not say how the attackers got in (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).
Detection
From the described behaviour: file-integrity monitoring on PHP configuration directories for any auto_prepend_file that points outside the application tree; shells or interpreters spawned by php-fpm or web server workers; writes to shell startup files, authorized_keys and any new sudo alias; PHP or web-server access to the mail store; new systemd units, five-minute cron entries and hidden-name SUID-root binaries; outbound WebSocket, GSocket or file-hosting connections from servers; touch -t changes, bursts of deleted history and mail logs, and pkill sequences that name EDR agents.

Triage: Plesk or PHP hardening can legitimately set auto_prepend_file and administrators do define sudo aliases; the report supports these discriminators: a prepended file with a vendor-like name outside the application tree, an alias that prompts for and logs the password, a log file named after another product, and red-team marker strings that no change record explains.

Defender takeaway
Audit every PHP configuration for auto_prepend_file, privileged accounts' startup files for a sudo alias and authorized_keys for unknown keys, and the file system for root-SUID binaries under hidden names; ship authentication, mail and web logs off-host so local log cleanup cannot erase them; patch PwnKit and keep Linux EDR self-protection alerting.
threat16 Oct 04:21Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42

item.title: Citizen Lab: spyware delivery through targeted ads, with defence and government networks among the impressions
item.description: Citizen Lab and Confiant report that Discover-Tech, an ad-tech firm, serves targeted ads whose code decides per device whether to return JavaScript, and that for chosen devices the chain hands off to servers Citizen Lab links with high confidence to Candiru spyware; at least 45 devices at Al Jazeera were targeted in 2024 and 2025. Citizen Lab's bidding data shows Discover-Tech ads on networks of defence ministries, armed forces, national cyber agencies and NATO, though an impression alone does not prove infection, and neither report mentions Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

AdFection: Citizen Lab and Confiant document zero-click Candiru spyware delivered through targeted online ads from the ad-tech firm Discover-Tech, with ad impressions on defence-ministry, armed-forces and NATO networks

Citizen Lab reports that in 2024 and 2025 at least 45 devices at the news network Al Jazeera were targeted in zero-click attacks that it links with high confidence to Candiru spyware delivered through ads bought by Discover-Tech, an Israeli firm that presents itself as an ad company (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). An ad carries a script tag that calls Discover-Tech's ad-decision server with the user's cookie or mobile advertising identifier; the server decides, apparently from the source address and the identifiers, whether the device is eligible, and returns JavaScript only if so and a zero-byte response otherwise, which keeps malicious code and pointers to it out of what ad vendors can inspect (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). In Al Jazeera's network logs an infected device first contacted Discover-Tech infrastructure, which indicates an ad impression, then a Candiru validator server that checks the device, and finally a Candiru command-and-control server; a Windows implant that Al Jazeera isolated from a compromised device and Citizen Lab analysed persists through COM hijacking (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Confiant, working from ad-delivery telemetry from April to September 2026, describes a cloaked payload that fingerprints the device and opens an encrypted channel, and found a hand-off to Candiru-attributed infrastructure, with Belgium by far the most targeted country at 56 percent of the global hits in the period; it has not captured a full exploit chain (Confiant, 2026-10-15).

Citizen Lab's analysis of four billion Discover-Tech bidding records shows ads on almost 200,000 websites and apps in four months, including on devices in networks of defence ministries, armed forces, national cyber agencies and intergovernmental organizations such as NATO; an impression alone does not prove targeting or infection (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Google, IAB Europe, Beeswax, Vungle (Liftoff) and Eskimi disconnected Discover-Tech after the disclosure (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Any device that renders third-party ads in a browser or an app, on staff whose phones or workstations an espionage buyer would want, such as defence, security and diplomatic staff; no source reports an infection in Switzerland, and neither report mentions it (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).
Detection
In per-device web-proxy, DNS and egress logs the reported signature is contact with Discover-Tech infrastructure, which marks an ad impression, followed by a connection to a validator server and finally to a command-and-control server, the sequence seen in Al Jazeera's network logs (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Confiant adds that the ad-delivered SDK resolves an operator-chosen domain over DNS-over-HTTPS and reaches it by raw IP, so it never appears as a plaintext DNS query or connection hostname and stays invisible to DNS-based monitoring and blocklists (Confiant, 2026-10-15). On a Windows endpoint, the implant Citizen Lab analysed persists through COM hijacking, so a new COM registration that points at an unfamiliar DLL is the artifact to look for.

Triage: ordinary ad tags also call identifier-bearing endpoints and sync user IDs; the reported discriminators are the eligibility gating, with an empty reply for ineligible devices and code only for chosen ones, and the validator-then-command-and-control sequence (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

Defender takeaway
The delivery is zero-click and needs no user action, and Citizen Lab says there is currently no consistently safe way to expose users and networks to targeted ads; its control is to block online advertising at the organization's gateway and on work-issued and edge devices (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

item.title: Drupal patches a critical Field UI RCE reachable through contributed modules; uninstall field_ui if you cannot update
item.description: Drupal's advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-108097, a remote code execution flaw in the core Field UI module rated Critical (19 of 25): core alone is not directly exploitable, but several exploit paths exist through contributed modules and at least one known path needs no login. Fixed releases are 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below and Drupal 8 and 9 get no fix, and until a site is updated the advisory's mitigation is to uninstall the Field UI module. The advisory records no public exploit at publication, and The Hacker News relays the Security Team's pre-announcement warning that exploits might be developed within hours or days.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-108097 +1NATOA2

CVE-2026-108097, Drupal core (SA-CORE-2026-014): a critical Field UI code-execution flaw reachable through contributed modules, at least one without login; fixed in 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19, with no fix for end-of-life branches (Drupal risk 19/25)

The Drupal Security Team's advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 of 2026-10-14 rates CVE-2026-108097 Critical, 19 out of 25 on Drupal's own scale, a remote code execution flaw in the core Field UI module: the vulnerability is not directly exploitable with core alone, but multiple serious exploit paths exist with contributed modules and at least one known path needs no authentication (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-14). The advisory names no module that opens a path; The Hacker News reads the mechanism from the fix, where Field UI's table element ran whatever PHP callable each row carried in its #region_callback property through call_user_func_array with no check, bypassing the renderer's rule against untrusted callbacks, and 11.4.10 no longer calls it (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

Fixed releases are Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below, and Drupal 8 and 9 are end of life and get no fix, which The Hacker News counts at 28.5 percent of the sites reporting a core version in the week of 2026-10-04 (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). The advisory records no public exploit at publication, but the Security Team's pre-announcement of 2026-10-12 told sites to reserve time "because exploits might be developed within hours or days", and in May Drupal reported exploit attempts within two days of a core SQL injection advisory that CISA then added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). The contributed Entity List module has its own critical code-execution advisory, SA-CONTRIB-2026-218, under the same conditions, at least one known path needing no authentication, and 3.0.10 fixes it (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-14); the flaw is CVE-2026-108099, and updating core does not update the module (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Drupal core on 10.6.x below 10.6.19, 11.3.x below 11.3.19 or 11.4.x below 11.4.10, or on an end-of-life branch from 8.9 to 11.2, with the Field UI module installed (the Standard install profile installs it) and a contributed module or custom code that exposes the vulnerable functionality, which the advisory does not name; Drupal Steward, a web application firewall service run by Acquia, Pantheon, Ironstar and Skpr, blocks some known vectors but not every one (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).
Detection
The advisory publishes no exploit artifact. The result of the flaw is PHP code running as the web server's user, so as an inference from that, watch web access logs for unusual requests to routes that contributed modules provide, PHP worker process lineage for shells, curl or interpreters spawned by the web server, and new or modified PHP files under the web root and the Drupal files directory. An exposed site updated only after the fix was public needs that file-integrity review in addition to the update.
Defender takeaway
Update core to the fixed release of its branch now, internet-facing sites first, because the flaw's mechanism is readable from the public fix and Drupal itself warned that exploits could follow within hours or days; where a site cannot be updated at once, uninstall Field UI, which removes the field management and display admin pages until the update (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). Custom code that set #region_callback on a field_ui_table row stops working after the update, so test the manage fields and manage display pages (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

item.title: BeyondTrust patches an exploited Remote Support zero-day; the actor's persistence survives reboot and reset
item.description: BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; all versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. Google's Threat Intelligence Group found ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploiting it as a zero-day in late August 2026, leaving a web shell, a root-SUID shell and a sudoers entry that survive reboot and configuration reset, so a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and a rebuild where its status is confirmed or unknown.
item.content:encoded:
CRITICALCVE-2026-102764exploitedNATOB1

CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation (CWE-290) in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; every version up to 26.2.3 is affected (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). Google's Threat Intelligence Group found in an incident response that ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploited the flaw as a zero-day in late August 2026 (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust dates the exploitation of one hosted instance and one self-hosted appliance to 2026-08-29 (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). GTIG warns that ARMORY CASTLE and others have historically exploited broadly once a flaw is public (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust lists government among the actor's documented targets (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

After the exploit GTIG saw SAWFLY, a lightweight PHP web shell that evaluates attacker-supplied code as the appliance's unprivileged site account; the actor then made a root-owned SUID copy of the system shell, tried to dump the appliance's native secrets vault, and persisted through a boot-time script that adds a passwordless-sudo line to the sudoers template, so the escalation survives reboot and configuration reset (GTIG, 2026-10-15). It deleted appliance logs throughout, raised an account's Jump Item and Team permissions from No Access to Administrator, pulled software inventories from users' desktops through the built-in file transfer, and exposed BARECLAW, a custom SOCKS5-over-WebSocket tunneler, by editing the HAProxy configuration (GTIG, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Self-hosted Remote Support appliances on any version up to 26.2.3 without the BT26-05-RS patch; the advisory says to apply the patch manually unless the instance is subscribed to automatic updates in its /appliance interface, and a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15), which closes the hole but does not undo earlier exposure (GTIG, 2026-10-15). SaaS tenants were patched by 2026-10-09 (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust patched Privileged Remote Access too, which shares the code, though it found no way to exploit it (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).
Detection
The actor deletes on-appliance logs, so use other copies: forwarded syslog for user changes that raise a Jump Item or Team role to Administrator and for account or API-account changes without a change ticket; authentication logs for administrative /login success from residential-broadband or commercial-VPN address space; reverse-proxy or WAF logs for unknown .php paths and WebSocket upgrades from non-support addresses; file transfers by accounts whose roles changed (GTIG, 2026-10-15). Patching does not evict the actor, so GTIG advises redeploying any appliance of confirmed or unknown status from a clean, fully patched image and then rotating credentials in dependency order, from the appliance administrators to anything typed into a support session (GTIG, 2026-10-15).

Triage: a known administrator changing Jump Item roles or signing in from a new network under a change ticket is routine; BeyondTrust's signals are privileged sessions from residential or VPN addresses tied to no administrator or ticket (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

Defender takeaway
Patch every self-hosted appliance now, then treat each one that was internet-reachable on an affected build since late August as potentially compromised until reviewed, and redeploy from a clean image any whose status is confirmed or unknown (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust adds that the built-in triage tool of its third-party detection platform closed the sensors' privilege-escalation alerts as false positives, and that it is working with the vendor so that automated triage cannot close high-severity signals on its own (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

item.title: Update: Adobe fixes unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce; no exploitation known
item.description: Sansec reproduced four code-execution routes for the Commerce and Magento flaw CVE-2026-103849 within 24 hours of Adobe's fix and expects attackers to do the same, though it has seen no attacks on live stores; it says a plain Composer install keeps the vulnerable base version until the 2026-oct release or Adobe's isolated patch is applied, and that the September StyleSmuggler hotfix must stay in place because the two fixes are separate.
item.content:encoded:
Update16 Oct 2026 04:13 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidenceverificationsourcing_noteactionsbody

Sansec reproduced four code-execution routes for the Commerce and Magento flaw CVE-2026-103849 within 24 hours of Adobe's fix and expects attackers to do the same, though it has seen no attacks on live stores; it says a plain Composer install keeps the vulnerable base version until the 2026-oct release or Adobe's isolated patch is applied, and that the September StyleSmuggler hotfix must stay in place because the two fixes are separate.

Sansec reports that it reproduced four different attack routes to code execution for the Commerce and Magento template-engine flaw CVE-2026-103849 within 24 hours of Adobe's fix and expects threat actors to do the same, and that it has not seen attacks on live stores (Sansec, 2026-10-15). It describes the flaw as a second-pass directive injection like September's StyleSmuggler, where attacker-controlled data in a child template can still be signed and re-scanned at the root level so that a smuggled block directive runs inside Magento's rendering, and says Adobe's October patch replaces that generic re-scan with registered placeholders (Sansec, 2026-10-15). Sansec questions Adobe's priority 2 rating for the Commerce bulletin, a 30-day patch window, because StyleSmuggler went from a priority 1 hotfix to mass exploitation in three days and it judges BlockStrap to be of similar complexity (Sansec, 2026-10-15).

Two cautions for the patch: a plain Composer install still has the vulnerable base version, so the 2026-oct release or Adobe's isolated patch must be applied, and BlockStrap and StyleSmuggler are separate fixes, so the September hotfix for CVE-2026-75650 has to stay in place as well (Sansec, 2026-10-15). Sansec lists Adobe Commerce up to 2.4.9, Adobe Commerce B2B up to 1.5.3 and Magento Open Source up to 2.4.9 as affected (Sansec, 2026-10-15).

Open finding: Adobe October 2026 bulletins: unauthenticated CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 flaws, most leading to code execution, in ColdFusion (APSB26-144), Experience Manager (APSB26-152) and Commerce and Magento (APSB26-153), none reported exploited →

item.title: Update: IDCF Cloud outage: backups now retrievable for 194 of 495 customers; provider finds no trace of server data taken

CISA added CVE-2026-21589 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15, "based on evidence of active exploitation" (CISA, 2026-10-15). The alert does not say what the evidence is, who is exploiting the flaw or whether any attempt succeeded, so neither CISA nor the honeypot operators report a compromise. Previdian's page, updated 2026-10-16, now counts 607 attempts from 65 unique addresses in 20 countries across five sensors between 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-15, and lists the flaw as in the CISA catalog (Previdian, 2026-10-16). NCSC Switzerland edited its advisory on 2026-10-12 to list the status as proof of concept available and actively exploited, citing the attempts Previdian recorded on its honeypot sensors (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-12).

item.title: Update: PK Softech: the City of Zurich pension fund confirms its test data was stolen; Pensionskasse Post says data left
item.description: Cantonal police warn that criminals could use the leaked salary and pension data to phone insured persons with investment-fraud offers, SwissCybersecurity.net ties the warning to PK Softech, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK says its PK Softech software runs in its own data centre so it is not directly affected; PK Softech can neither confirm nor rule out further affected customers, and the Ticino fund listed as a customer has made no statement.
item.content:encoded:
Update16 Oct 2026 04:11 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Cantonal police warn that criminals could use the leaked salary and pension data to phone insured persons with investment-fraud offers, SwissCybersecurity.net ties the warning to PK Softech, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK says its PK Softech software runs in its own data centre so it is not directly affected; PK Softech can neither confirm nor rule out further affected customers, and the Ticino fund listed as a customer has made no statement.

On the Cybercrimepolice platform, dated 2026-10-13, the cantonal police warn that after a cyberattack on a software provider of a pension fund, criminals could use the leaked personal and financial data to phone those affected and lure them into fraudulent investments of their pension assets (translated from German); the page describes a ransomware attack at the end of September and names no company (Cybercrimepolice, 2026-10-13). SwissCybersecurity.net ties the warning to PK Softech, names the cantonal police of Zurich and Bern as its authors, and reads its conditional wording as meaning no case of actual misuse had been registered yet (SwissCybersecurity.net, 2026-10-15). The police ask pension funds to tell insured persons that knowing someone's personal details or the size of their pension assets is no proof that a caller is trustworthy, and to let them check enquiries through official channels (Cybercrimepolice, 2026-10-13).

The Zurich cantonal fund BVK, which insures the cantonal administration and has bought PK Softech software since 2011, says through its spokesperson that the application runs in the BVK's own data centre independently of the supplier, so it is from today's view not directly affected, and that PK Softech holds only working material from it such as documentation, troubleshooting reports and further-development concepts (translated from German; NZZ, 2026-10-13). PK Softech told the NZZ that it can neither confirm nor rule out that further customers are affected and left the question whether a ransom was demanded unanswered (NZZ, 2026-10-13). Inside IT adds that the Istituto di previdenza del Cantone Ticino is listed on the Simap procurement platform as a PK Softech customer since 2018 and has made no statement on whether its data is at risk (Inside IT, 2026-10-14).

Open finding: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating →

item.title: Update: Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure chain: its root step had no fix at disclosure, and it evades the Integrity Checker
item.description: CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. CERT-FR also counts 25.1.3.0 as affected, so the fixed-build targets now name 25.1.3.1.
item.content:encoded:
Update16 Oct 2026 04:10 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelsummaryimmediate_actioncvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. CERT-FR also counts 25.1.3.0 as affected, so the fixed-build targets now name 25.1.3.1.

CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says Ivanti reports the vulnerability as actively exploited and that CERT-FR itself is aware of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). It puts the response in an order: fully isolate the appliance from both the internet and the internal network, snapshot the file system and memory of a virtual appliance, avoid powering it off so that traces survive, place the logs under seal and analyse the appliance with the Volexity indicators, and only then, on compromise, factory-reset it, upgrade and reset the secrets (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). Its list of secrets to treat as compromised is wider than a password reset: the LDAP and Active Directory secrets, every certificate on the appliance (machine, user-authentication, code-signing and the TLS certificate of the exposed interface), the administration password, stored API keys, the passwords of local accounts including the service accounts used for authentication servers, the Kerberos tickets and other authentication material of those service accounts, and the licence-server authentication (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). CERT-FR adds that running Ivanti's external Integrity Checker Tool needs physical access to the appliance and can interrupt service, and that some threats survive a factory reset (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). Its affected-systems list names the 22.8Rx builds before 22.8R2.5, the 25.1.1.x builds before 25.1.1.2 and the 25.1.3.x builds before 25.1.3.1 and does not list a 25.1.2.x line; by counting 25.1.3.x builds before 25.1.3.1 as affected it includes 25.1.3.0, a build that Rapid7's table lists as resolved (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14).

Open finding: CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, and the root-escalation step of the chain was unpatched at disclosure (CVSS 8.6) →

item.title: Update: Ahsay admits its earlier AhsayCBS patches were incomplete; the hotfixes are partner-only and CISA lists both flaws as exploited
item.description: Ahsay says its previous patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully fix the flaws and names the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 and v9.15.2.70, available only to partners; Huntress verified the v10 hotfix, CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14, and Bitdefender MDR describes three intrusions through the chain. Hotfixes now cover v10 and v7 to v9, through the partner portal.
item.content:encoded:
Update16 Oct 2026 04:09 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryprioritytagstechniquescvessourcesevidenceverificationsourcing_noteconfidenceclassificationactionsbody

Ahsay says its previous patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully fix the flaws and names the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 and v9.15.2.70, available only to partners; Huntress verified the v10 hotfix, CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14, and Bitdefender MDR describes three intrusions through the chain. Hotfixes now cover v10 and v7 to v9, through the partner portal.

Ahsay now says its previous patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 "did not fully address" the two flaws, and tells partners to apply the AhsayCBS v10.3.4.45 hotfix on v10 and the v9.15.2.70 hotfix on v7, v8 and v9, both from the partner portal (a valid partner login is required), then to reboot the server (Ahsay, 2026-10-12). The announcement is dated 2026-10-12; Huntress, in an update of the same day to its report, dates the hotfix release to that day and says it independently verified that the v10.3.4.45 hotfix mitigates the initial entry point of the chain, which was still open on earlier v10 versions (Huntress, 2026-10-08).

CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14 "based on evidence of active exploitation" (CISA, 2026-10-14). Bitdefender MDR reports three intrusions through the chain, the first two beginning around 7 to 8 October and a third identified on 14 October; in the first, attackers validated access through JSP webshells, staged PowerShell payloads, tried to stage payloads as command files in C:\Users\Public and tried to establish persistence; in the second they deployed JSP files, tried the same command-file staging, searched for stored credentials, elevated an account to SYSTEM and used obfuscated PowerShell to install and configure OpenSSH, which gives a way back that does not depend on the vulnerable web service, so patching alone does not end the incident; across its incidents the follow-on PowerShell scripts were staged on a subdomain of a public static-site hosting service; it attributes the activity to no named actor, and notes that the file names, tools and binaries differed from one incident to the next, so the dependable signal is how the server behaves after the exploit fires (Bitdefender, 2026-10-15).

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

Censys, which scans for Danfoss StoreView control panels, says Danfoss has not confirmed the initial access vector and points to three AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier: CVE-2025-41450 (March 2025), which Censys describes as letting an unauthenticated actor log in as an administrator with a code computed from the current calendar date, and CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452 (August 2025), which it says let authenticated users run commands and disrupt the management interface (Censys, 2026-10-14). Censys maps the firmware by build: below 4.2 carries all three, 4.2.4 fixes only the date-based login and still carries the two later ones, and 4.3.1 or later fixes all three (Censys, 2026-10-14). Its scan counted 1,825 exposed StoreView panels in France on 2026-10-11 and 537 on 2026-10-14, a fall of 71 percent, with builds below 4.2, build 4.2.4 and builds from 4.3.1 leaving at about the same rate, which it reads as operators taking controllers off the internet rather than patching them (Censys, 2026-10-14). Outside France the count fell from 1,166 to 966, and in ten of the twelve countries with the most exposed hosts more than 60 percent of the hosts run a build below 4.3.1, led by Poland at 81 percent and Romania at 80 percent (Censys, 2026-10-14).

item.title: Huntress: a lookalike VPN-client site harvests credentials, then hands over the real signed installer
item.description: Huntress describes a lookalike WatchGuard VPN download site, reached on 2026-10-07 by an administrator at a managed service provider through a Bing search result, that asks for the SSL VPN server, login and password, rejects the first submission so the victim types again, and only then downloads the genuine, validly signed WatchGuard installer from WatchGuard's own CDN. No malware is delivered, so endpoint controls have no file to flag, and few reputation engines flagged the domains.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

A fake WatchGuard VPN download site captures the SSL VPN server, login and password in the browser and then serves the genuine signed installer, leaving no malicious file for endpoint tools to flag

Huntress's SOC investigated an incident on 2026-10-07 in which an administrator at a managed service provider searched Bing for a WatchGuard VPN download with a typo in the query and clicked through the standard Bing result redirect to a lookalike site titled "WatchGuard Firebox VPN Client", which Huntress classes as search-engine poisoning rather than malvertising (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Choosing any download option opens a pop-up asking for Server, Login and Password; one unobfuscated JavaScript file of about 150 lines posts the typed values as JSON to a separate collector domain, tagged as the first or second attempt, and always rejects the first submission with an "incorrect data" message so that the victim types again or tries a second set of credentials (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Only after the second submission does the page fetch the real WatchGuard Mobile VPN with SSL installer from WatchGuard's own CDN, an Authenticode-signed file whose digest Huntress recomputed and found unmodified, so there is no trojanized installer or malicious DLL for endpoint defenses to flag (Huntress, 2026-10-13). The victim's browser history showed no download in the observed window, so Huntress judges the user probably did not finish both rounds but may have typed credentials in the first, and Managed Defender flagged the incident 21 seconds after the lookalike domain loaded (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Both domains were registered within the previous two months, few reputation engines flagged either as of 2026-10-08, and the lure domain was offline by 2026-10-13 (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Huntress places the iteration in a campaign that WatchGuard's Secplicity team described in January 2026 as lookalike download sites for WatchGuard, F5, Fortinet, SonicWall and Sophos clients, and that Microsoft tied in March 2026 to a financially motivated actor it tracks as Storm-2561; the new element is that the fake client is gone from the middle (Huntress, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
Administrators and users who find an SSL VPN client through a web search, as an administrator at a managed service provider did here; the lure here impersonates WatchGuard, and Huntress describes the same campaign against clients of five vendors (Huntress, 2026-10-13). The credentials of any VPN account typed into such a page, and the gateway address with them, are in the attacker's hands.
Detection
No malicious file or process reaches the endpoint, so the signal is in web proxy and DNS telemetry (a visit that arrives from a search-result redirect to a domain that is not the vendor's, followed by a JSON POST to a second, recently registered domain; Huntress's Managed Defender did flag the browsing activity) and in VPN gateway authentication logs; Huntress advises watching for SSL VPN logins from hosting providers, unfamiliar ASNs and countries where the account has never connected (Huntress, 2026-10-13).

Triage: a genuine VPN client also asks for server, login and password, but only inside the installed client at connect time; a browser form that collects the three values before any installer has run, on a domain that is not the vendor's, is the signal.

Defender takeaway
If a user typed VPN credentials into a page found through search, reset every affected account and treat the VPN endpoint those credentials belong to as known to the attacker; enforce multi-factor authentication on the VPN, and publish and bookmark the official client download links in internal documentation so staff do not search for them (Huntress, 2026-10-13).

item.title: Exploited Nextcloud Collabora CODE app flaw: disabling the app does not help; update to 26.4.303 or remove it
item.description: CVE-2026-110447 is an OS command injection in proxy.php of the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server, the richdocumentscode app that runs Collabora inside Nextcloud; versions before 26.4.303 are affected, the GitHub advisory record says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026, and a hoster reported web shells on its Nextcloud servers on 2026-09-11. Disabling the app does not stop the request, so it must be updated to 26.4.303 or removed; standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-110447exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-110447, Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server (Nextcloud richdocumentscode app): an unauthenticated command injection in proxy.php, exploited in the wild to plant PHP web shells, fixed in 26.4.303 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

Collabora's own advisory, published 2026-10-14, says users of Nextcloud with the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) can be vulnerable through proxy.php: a request can run an operating system command as the web server user, the attack works only while the built-in CODE server is not running (after a restart, an upgrade or a crash), and disabling the app is not sufficient, it must be upgraded to 26.4.303 or later or removed (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14). Users of end-of-life Nextcloud 29 or older should upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app, standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected, and the fix for CVE-2025-66208 does not prevent this flaw (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14). The GitHub Advisory Database record for CVE-2026-110447 says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-14). Field reports came first: on 2026-09-11 a hoster reported on the app's issue tracker that several Nextcloud servers running richdocumentscode 26.4.302 had been compromised since the previous day through requests to proxy.php that carried shell command substitution and an encoded path traversal, with base64 payloads decoded and run through a shell to create PHP web shells in the app directory; on one server the attacker then searched for password-manager databases and cryptocurrency-wallet files, and the reviewed requests showed no archiving or upload commands (issue 354, 2026-09-11). Other administrators report the same compromise, one noticing it because Nextcloud's integrity check failed on an unexpected PHP file (issue 354, 2026-09-11). A reply on the issue says the flaw affects only the Development Edition in the Built-in CODE Server mode that downloads a local AppImage, and a later one that leftover web-shell files must be removed after upgrading (issue 354, 2026-09-11). A Nextcloud forum post of 2026-10-03 told users to update, saying that as far as the poster knew no CVE existed (Nextcloud community forum, 2026-10-03).

Exposure
A Nextcloud server with the "Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server" app at 26.4.302 or older, including one patched for CVE-2025-66208; a restart, an upgrade or a crash that stops the built-in CODE server opens the window, and deactivating the app does not close it (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14).
Detection
In web access logs, requests to the app's proxy.php whose path carries $( command substitution and an encoded ..; in file telemetry, unexpected PHP files in the app directory, which Nextcloud's integrity check flagged on a compromised server; in process telemetry, the web server account starting a shell that decodes base64 and calls out with curl or wget to an external service (issue 354, 2026-09-11). The web shell survives the update, so the post-patch check is the same file and process search, and the reporter says secrets available to the web server account must be treated as potentially affected (issue 354, 2026-09-11).
Defender takeaway
Update the app to 26.4.303 or remove it on every Nextcloud server that has it, because disabling it does not stop the request, and on Nextcloud 29 or older upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14); then search for dropped PHP files and the request pattern back to at least early September 2026, and on a hit rotate whatever the web server account can read (issue 354, 2026-09-11).

item.title: Palo Alto confirms limited exploitation of a PAN-OS management-interface root flaw; no workaround, 11.2.16 now published
item.description: Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection in the PAN-OS management interface that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the advisory is tagged as attacked and reports very limited exploitation, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. There is no workaround and the risk is highest where the management interface is reachable from the internet; 11.2.16, the fixed build for units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15, was published on 2026-10-15, so every train now has a fixed build.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-0322exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-0322, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS: code injection in the management interface gives an authenticated attacker root, exploited in very limited attacks and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS-B 8.6)

Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 describes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection (CWE-94) in the management interface of PAN-OS that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run arbitrary code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series); Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected and no special configuration is needed to be affected (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). The advisory is tagged as attacked and says very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the management interface (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14), and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day (CISA, 2026-10-14). Palo Alto scores it CVSS-B 8.6 with a suggested urgency of highest, says the risk is highest when the management interface is reachable from the internet, and scores it 8.5 when access is restricted to a single jump box (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). It lists no workaround; Threat Prevention IDs 510046 and 510047 give limited coverage and only when management traffic is routed through a data-plane interface and decrypted, and Palo Alto warns that variations of the attack may not be detected (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Fixes ship per train; a unit on 11.2.14 or 11.2.15 had no fixed build when the advisory appeared, and 11.2.16, the fix for those two releases, was published on 2026-10-15 (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). The advisory does not say how the attackers obtained the credentials the flaw requires, when exploitation began or who is behind it, and BleepingComputer says it asked Palo Alto when exploitation began, who is behind the attacks and whether attackers compromised firewalls or used them to reach internal networks (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-14).

Exposure
Any PA-Series or VM-Series firewall or Panorama (virtual or M-Series) on PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 or 12.2 below the fixed build of its train, with no configuration needed; the exposure is greatest where the management interface accepts connections from outside trusted internal addresses (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). BleepingComputer reads the advisory as requiring existing credentials and network access to the management interface (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-14).
Detection
Look at authentication and administrator-change records on the management interface, and at inbound connections to the management address in upstream firewall or provider logs, for logins from unfamiliar sources; Palo Alto's advisory FAQ lists three source addresses associated with the limited exploit attempts to compare against (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Root code execution means an upgrade does not evict an attacker who is already in, and the advisory gives no file or process artifact, so a device that was reachable from untrusted networks before the fix needs a compromise assessment as well as the patch.
Defender takeaway
Take the management interface off every network but trusted internal addresses, with a jump box as the tightest setting Palo Alto describes, and upgrade to the fixed build of each train; units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15 upgrade to 11.2.16, which Palo Alto published on 2026-10-15 (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14).

item.title: Cisco's mail gateway has a second exploited root flaw in four weeks; the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update
item.description: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools earlier than 25.3.0.5525 are exposed; there is no workaround, and the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update that needs no restart or upgrade, and in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780.
item.content:encoded:
CRITICALCVE-2026-76519exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-76519, Cisco Secure Email Gateway: one crafted email attachment writes files and runs commands as root, exploited in the wild and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 9.8)

Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 describes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway: improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled lets an unauthenticated remote attacker who sends a crafted attachment through the device write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system and run commands as root, and Cisco rates it CVSS 3.1 9.8 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Cisco states that in October 2026 its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation, and that it has directly contacted Cisco Secure Email Cloud customers on whose devices indicators of possible compromise were identified (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14); CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day (CISA, 2026-10-14). Cisco gives no workaround; the fix is distributed through the Content Scanner Tools package for every supported AsyncOS release and needs no software upgrade or restart, and it is also in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780, while release 16.0 must migrate to a fixed release (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). It is the second exploited root-level flaw in this product in about four weeks: BleepingComputer notes that last month Cisco warned of CVE-2026-76461, which also lets unauthenticated remote attackers run commands as root (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-14).

Exposure
A physical or virtual Cisco Secure Email Gateway is exposed when both conditions hold: the File Reputation service is enabled and assigned to a mail policy (web interface, Mail Policies, Incoming or Outgoing Mail Policies, Advanced Malware Protection, "Enable File Reputation" ticked), and the Content Scanner Tools version, shown by the contentscannerstatus command, is earlier than 25.3.0.5525; Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not affected, and Cisco Secure Email Cloud Gateway customers need take no action (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). The attack arrives as an email attachment passing through the appliance, so exposure does not depend on its management interface being reachable (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14).
Detection
Start with the appliance's own logs: Cisco's self-check is grep "System Security" system_logs on each cluster member, which returns "Suspected compromise indicator was found", "Security scan did not complete" or "No compromise indicator was found" (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Cisco warns that an attacker with root may remove or hide evidence, so it also recommends cross-checking network and firewall logs outside the device for unexpected uploads from the appliance to external addresses or downloads from malicious addresses (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14); that is egress telemetry from the gateway's own addresses.
Defender takeaway
Confirm Content Scanner Tools 25.3.0.5525 or later on every gateway today, since automatic updates deliver it and only gateways with updates disabled need the manual update, and run the log check on every one; for a virtual appliance with a compromise indicator, Cisco says to keep forensic data before upgrading, because upgrading a compromised instance destroys it, then deploy a new virtual machine on a fixed release, rebuild the configuration without importing an old file and renew credentials and cryptographic material (a physical appliance goes to Cisco TAC), and strongly recommends restoring every member of a cluster that contains a compromised appliance, since the cluster's SSH private keys could be accessed (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14).

CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units.
